import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str,expected",
    [
        (None, None),                         # None input
        ("", ""),                             # Empty string
        ("plain text", "plain text"),         # No ampersand
        ("&", "&"),                       # Single known entity
        ("a & b", "a & b"),               # Single entity in context
        ("a & b < c > d", "a & b < c > d"),  # Multiple entities
        ("&&", "&&"),                 # Double ampersand should stay unchanged
        ("&foo;", "&foo;"),                   # Unknown entity stays unchanged
        ("&amp", "&amp"),                     # Missing semicolon stays unchanged
        ("&foo;", "&foo;"),           # Entity followed by extra text and semicolon
        ("&<", "&<&"),                 # Adjacent entities
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_basic_cases(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_edge_lengths():
    # Length zero (empty string)
    assert unescapeHTML("") == ""

    # Length one (single character, not an entity)
    assert unescapeHTML("x") == "x"

    # Length two (possible start of an entity but incomplete)
    assert unescapeHTML("&a") == "&a"

    # Length three (still incomplete)
    assert unescapeHTML("&am") == "&am"

    # Length four (still incomplete, no trailing semicolon)
    assert unescapeHTML("&amp") == "&amp"

    # Length five (complete entity)
    assert unescapeHTML("&") == "&"

    # Longer string with many characters but no entities
    long_str = "a" * 1000
    assert unescapeHTML(long_str) == long_str

    # Long string with many entities interleaved
    long_entities = ("&" * 250) + ("<" * 250)
    expected = ("&" * 250) + ("<" * 250)
    assert unescapeHTML(long_entities) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_no_regression_on_double_ampersand():
    # Old implementation would not match the second '&' as part of an entity.
    # Ensure the new implementation still leaves this pattern unchanged.
    input_str = "&& &< &unknown; &amp"
    expected = "&& &< &unknown; &amp"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_mixed_content():
    # Mixed content with valid, unknown, and malformed entities
    input_str = "Start & middle &unknown; end &lt"
    expected = "Start & middle &unknown; end &lt"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
